newsitem.title: UK: Unilever plans more streamlining - paper.
newsitem.headline: Unilever plans more streamlining - paper.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever is set to streamline further its businesses in a move to enhance shareholder value under new UK chairman Niall Fitzgerald, the Sunday Times reported.
The newspaper said the group plans to "cull" businesses accounting for up to seven billion stg of annual sales, nearly 20 percent of its total.
"We have 57 categories but fewer than 20 are of strategic importance or substantial local importance," the newspaper quoted Fitzgerald as saying.

It also quoted what it said was a "newly-drafted mission statement" from the group as saying the company will seek "sustainable profitable growth for our businesses and long-term value creation for our shareholders and employees."

Unilever's trading profit in 1995 was unchanged from a year earlier at 2.5 billion stg. In the three months ended June 30 this year, Unilever Plc's profit before tax was 616 million stg, down from 646 million a year earlier, with earnings per share of 19.39 pence against 21.91.
"We have immense growth opportunities which we haven't been exploiting, particularly in emerging markets," the newspaper quoted Fitzgerald as saying.
No spokesman from Unilever was immediately available to comment on the report.
